short: A Scottish Jacobite victory over government forces that cost the life of their commander.
full:
On 27 July 1689, a Jacobite army composed largely of Highland clansmen ambushed a government force commanded by General Hugh Mackay at the Pass of Killiecrankie in Perthshire. The Highlanders unleashed a devastating charge that broke the government lines in minutes, inflicting heavy casualties and routing the opposition.

However, the Jacobite commander, John Graham of Claverhouse, Viscount Dundee, was killed in the final moments of the assault. His death deprived the rising of its most capable leader, and without him the Highland forces lacked strategic direction. Their rebellion ultimately stalled, culminating in their defeat at the Battle of Dunkeld the following month.
